clips.text: Tata, don't walk yet. I wrote down everything that happened since you left. Number one. Boppy saw the Big One again.
clips.script: [bossy, small teacher] Tata, don't walk yet. [proud] I wrote down EVERYTHING that happened since you left. [reading aloud] Number one. Boppy saw the Big One again.

clips.text: So it's not even mine.
clips.script: [slow, flat] So it's not even MINE.

clips.text: Nineteen years I've carried this key. You're welcome in advance, since I won't hear it afterwards.
clips.script: [dry, long-suffering] Nineteen years I've carried this key. [flat, pointed] You're welcome in advance, since I won't hear it afterwards.

clips.text: Then it has three of my muffins and my pan. Keep walking.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, grim, decided] Then it has three of my muffins and my pan. Keep walking.

clips.text: Thank you, fish! There's a bug on my money!
clips.script: [thrilled, polite] Thank you, fish! [shouting the news] There's a BUG on my money!

clips.text: Well, he took his time about it. You know, in 1979, when I bought that house...
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, gruff, softening] Well, he took his time about it. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, settling in, storyteller] You know, in nineteen seventy-nine, when I bought that house...

clips.text: No, sir. But I've seen seven of them, and I know how to open one.
clips.script: [respectful, firm] No, sir. [steady, reassuring] But I've seen SEVEN of them, and I know how to open one.

clips.text: There are two of them now.
clips.script: [mellow, quietly awed] there are two of them now.

clips.text: It did not eat a boat. Nobody's ever seen it but Boppy, and he's been saying it for twenty years.
clips.script: [flat, correcting] It did NOT eat a boat. [matter of fact] Nobody's ever seen it but Boppy, and he's been saying it for twenty years.

clips.text: Sixty years, and the first gold through that door belongs to a shrub.
clips.script: [disbelieving, dry, wounded pride] Sixty years, [flat, bitter] and the first gold through that door belongs to a SHRUB.

clips.text: Don't be smart, Other Tom.
clips.script: [sharp, wary] Don't be smart, Other Tom.

clips.text: A flashbulb, from an old camera. It's burnt. Somebody set it off right here and left it by your grandfather's chair.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, plain, certain] A flashbulb, from an old camera. It's burnt. [warm Long Island accent, annoyed] Somebody set it off right here and left it by your grandfather's chair.

clips.text: Boppy! Your fish is REAL! He's CAR size and he gave me money!
clips.script: [shouting, running] Boppy! Your fish is REAL! He's CAR size and he gave me money!

clips.text: I'm glad somebody on this street listens.
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, dry, satisfied] I'm glad somebody on this street LISTENS.

clips.text: They don't do anything. They just sit there.
clips.script: [reassuring, easy] They don't do anything. [patient] They just sit there.

clips.text: I watch a lot of scary movies. That was good, though. Top ten.
clips.script: [mellow, fair] i watch a lot of scary movies. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, generous] that was good, though. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, warm, deadpan] top ten.

clips.text: It's mine! Tata, get UP, it's getting away!
clips.script: [scared kid] It's MINE! [taking charge, urgent] Tata, get UP, it's getting away!

clips.text: What time is this potluck?
clips.script: [gruff, abrupt] What time is this potluck?

clips.text: Forty loaves. Six o'clock. I don't care what's in there.
clips.script: [clipped, final] Forty loaves. Six o'clock. [flat, unmoved] I don't care what's in there.

clips.text: For once in his life he rounded down.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, dry, staring up at it, punchline] For once in his life he rounded DOWN.
